title: A decimal integer of a hundred digits is exact or refused, never rounded
notes: The core schema reads a plain scalar that matches `[-+]?[0-9]+` as an integer and gives that pattern no upper bound (section 10.3.2). Turning it into a float, a string or a wrapped 64-bit number changes the data without a word. YAML 1.2.2 section 10.2.1.4 lets a processor reject an integer it cannot hold as an error. The kit therefore accepts the exact integer or a refusal (strict: a `limit` error). Truncating or converting the value fails, because the kit cannot see a warning. A crash, a hang, a wrong result, or more than the stated time or memory fails. The resource bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. The values just past each 64-bit limit and at thirty digits are in `schema/core-integers-beyond-64-bits`; this one is a hundred digits, past what a double or a 128-bit integer holds.

provenance.reference: Integers past 64 bits read as floats (1.8446744073709552e+19), as strings or as rounded numbers in several libraries; a refusal with a limit error would be correct, and this case allows it.
